data.name: Arjant
data.gender_notes: Arjant is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Arjant is derived from the Sanskrit word 'Arjuna', meaning resplendent or golden. In Hindu mythology, Arjuna was a great warrior and a central character in the Mahabharata epic. The name Arjant carries the meaning “Golden, Resplendent” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Arjant usually hope their child will grow to embody golden, resplendent and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Arjant belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Golden, Resplendent.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Arjant total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

historical_references.reference: Arjuna, a prominent character in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, was also known as Arjant. Arjuna was a great warrior and was a member of the Pandava clan. He was the son of King Indra and the warrior prince Bhishma's niece, Subhadra. Arjuna was a central figure in the great Kurukshetra war, which occurred around 3100-2900 BCE and was fought between the Pandava and Kaurava clans for the throne of Hastinapura.

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Arjant is found in the ancient Jain text, the Agni Purana. This text mentions a king named Arjant Chakravartin, who was an ideal Jain ruler. Arjant is said to have ruled over the entire world during the era of the 22nd Tirthankara, Neminatha, around 1200 BCE. Arjant is known for his great piety and his devotion to Jainism, and is considered a model of Jain kingship.
